clues: This city lies in the heart of Argentina, in low hills by a river. The big port of Buenos Aires sits far to its southeast.
When heat waves make nights hot and sticky, south winds bring relief. Storms roll in, and a day or two of cool, crisp air breaks the heat.
A Spanish captain set up this town on 6 July 1573. He gave it the same name as a famed old city back in Spain.
Its school for higher study is the oldest in the land, set up in 1613. Folks call this place the learned one for its bookish past.
A group of old church and school blocks here is a World Heritage Site. UNESCO named the old Jesuit Block a prize site in the year 2000.
